# Code review — trusted reference-deployment startup (base a56254d, tree 144f278)

Scope verified: all three new files read in full, the full twelve-file patch read in full, plus the changed regions and the helpers they depend on (`development-contracts.ts` `administrativeData`/`administrativeArray`, `development-authority.ts` `DEVELOPMENT_OWNER_LIMITS`, `installed-reference-configuration.ts`, `transaction-installed-configuration.ts`, `transaction-runtime-configuration.ts` incl. local `fields`/`captureSeams`/`readOptions`, `protocol/src/json-admission.ts` decoder/`mapLosslessJson`/`admitJsonNumbers`, `config/src/index.ts` `StartupConfig`/`rawRead`/section assembly/`redactStartupConfig`).

There **are** concrete findings; none is a boundary breach of items 1–6, and I found no correctness or containment defect in the N1 depth/node correction.

## Findings

**1. Medium — nested `bdptest` allowlist cannot accept the real config section.**
`packages/server/src/reference-deployment.ts:150` validates with `fields(own.bdptest, [], ["fixture"])`. The section it is meant to receive is now `{fixture?, deploymentFile?}` (`packages/config/src/index.ts:82`, built at `:570-573`). Every other `ReferenceDeploymentInput` member is a byte-for-byte pass-through of a config section (`server` matches `:67-80` exactly; `scope` matches `:65`), so a caller will forward `config.bdptest` — and whenever `deploymentFile` is set (i.e. the only case where this loader runs) the key is outside the allowlist and the load fails with a blanket `"configuration"` refusal. The fixture-conflict guard is therefore unusable in exactly the configuration it exists for. TypeScript does not catch it: `{fixture?: string; deploymentFile?: string}` is structurally assignable to `{fixture?: string}` when passed as a variable.
